questions.exp: Hypovolemic/Hemorrhagic Shock: m/c type of shock. (Book p37)

questions.q: Concealed hemorrhage is:

questions.exp: Venous bleed: Hypotension occurs late (d/t compensation). (Book p37)

units.title: Hypovolemic Shock: Types & Head-Injury Notes
units.guide: Hypovolemic/hemorrhagic shock is the m/c shock: overt bleeding is easy to catch while concealed bleeding hides in neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis and long bones. An isolated head injury never causes it, so a hypotensive head-injury patient makes you suspect brain herniation, neurogenic shock above T6 or polytrauma.

units.title: Arterial vs Venous Bleed
units.guide: Arterial bleeds spurt, drop the pressure early and are prevented early; lacerated arteries bleed more because vasoconstriction widens the tear, while a clean transection bleeds less. Venous bleeds ooze gradually and hide hypotension late behind compensation.

units.title: Hemorrhage in Surgery
units.guide: Primary hemorrhage bleeds during surgery, reactionary hemorrhage within 24 hours from a dislodged clot or slipped granny's knot, and secondary hemorrhage after 7-14 days when infection sloughs the vessel wall.

units.title: Classification of Hypovolemic Shock
units.guide: Four classes climb from 0-15% (0.5 L, all normal, oral liquids) through 15-30% (1 L, tachycardia, anxious and thirsty) and 30-40% (1.5 L, falling SBP, confused, decompensated) to >40% (>2 L, non-recordable pulse and BP, anuria, coma, massive transfusion).

units.title: Compensated Shock & Fluid Response Check
units.guide: Class II is compensated shock: sympathetic noradrenaline and adrenaline drive tachycardia - the earliest sign - with peripheral vasoconstriction shunting blood to vital organs, cold extremities and raised peripheral resistance. Give 500 mL-1 L crystalloid and check the response.

units.title: Dynamic Fluid Response & Resuscitation Strategies
units.guide: Responders keep their improved PR, SBP and JVP; transient responders worsen after 15-20 minutes and non responders never improve - both mean ongoing losses. Before hemostasis use damage control resuscitation (damage control surgery, permissive hypotension, 1:1 RBC:FFP, tranexamic acid/platelets/fibrinogen); after hemostasis switch to perfusion-targeted resuscitation with pressors, thromboprophylaxis and end-organ monitoring.

units.title: Occult Hypoperfusion & Monitoring Indicators
units.guide: Occult hypoperfusion hides behind normal HR, SBP and urine output but betrays itself with low MVOS and acidosis. PCWP (Swan-Ganz, left heart, more accurate but difficult) outranks CVP (right heart, m/c used) for initial fluid requirement, while urine output (>0.5 mL/kg/hr adult, >1 mL/kg/hr child) is the best resuscitation indicator.

units.title: Shock Indices
units.guide: Shock index = HR/SBP with >0.9 meaning higher mortality; the modified shock index = HR/MAP is the most sensitive; ROPE = HR/pulse pressure with <3 stable and >3 warning of decompensated shock.

units.title: Monitors for Organ/Systemic Perfusion
units.guide: Base deficit and lactate flag acidosis for systemic perfusion while MVOS is the best end point of resuscitation. Muscle reads NIRS and tissue oxygen electrodes, gut mucosa - the most sensitive, forming stress ulcers - reads sublingual capnometry, mucosal pH and laser doppler, kidney reads urine output and brain reads consciousness with tissue oxygen electrode/NIRS.

units.title: Massive Blood Transfusion & Complications
units.guide: Massive transfusion = whole circulating volume or >10 units in 24 hrs or >4 units in one hour. It brings hypothermia, citrate-driven hypocalcemia/hypomagnesemia and metabolic alkalosis, hyperkalemia from lysed stored RBCs, and coagulopathy - the m/c cause of death - prevented by limiting crystalloids and giving 1:1:1 PRBC:platelet:FFP; febrile reactions are m/c overall and leukoreduction filters prevent them.

units.title: TACO vs TRALI
units.guide: TACO is cardiac overload with facial puffiness, pedal edema, breathlessness but a normal X-ray, treated with Lasix. TRALI is anti-HLA antibody driven non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema within 6 hours from multiparous donors or FFP, showing ARDS and patchy infiltrates.

units.title: Transfusion Criteria, Blood Substitutes & Anti-shock Garment
units.guide: Transfuse below Hb 6, individualise 6-8 with ongoing losses or impending surgery, and withhold above 8 without risk factors. Perfluorocarbon and stroma free hemoglobin were first and second generation; PEG hemoglobin, Hemospan (MP4OX) and PHP are next generation, and the anti-shock garment squeezes the legs hardest to hold up rural PPH patients.
